cs.label: Lula vyhraje druhé kolo v Brazílii
cs.text: Lula získá ve druhém kole brazilských prezidentských voleb 25. října 2026 více platných hlasů než Flávio Bolsonaro, podle výsledků TSE.
cs.criterion: ANO, pokud výsledky TSE (resultados.tse.jus.br / tse.jus.br) zveřejněné do 26. října 2026 12:00 SEČ ukážou, že Lula získal ve druhém kole prezidentských voleb více platných hlasů než Flávio Bolsonaro (při 100 % sečtených okrsků, nebo podle posledního údaje TSE v termínu, je-li výsledek matematicky rozhodnut). NE, pokud více hlasů získá Flávio Bolsonaro, nebo pokud se hlasování odloží či TSE do termínu výsledek nezveřejní.

base_rate.class: poll-lead model, Brazil runoff (lead Lula−Flávio −1.33 pp, sd 1.345 = rms Datafolha runoff lead error)

notes.base-rate: Poll-lead model with lead -1.3 and the pooled rms error of 2.734 (the Datafolha-only n=3 sd of 1.345 is too narrow) gives 0.31. Adjusted -0.15 log-odds because Brazilian polls have tended to underrate the right (2022: Datafolha lead error +2.2 toward Lula) and Flávio led the first round, then x0.99 for slip.
notes.evidence: Freshest polls have Flávio narrowly ahead (Quaest/PoderData 51-49, three-poll lead -1.3), with Datafolha trending to Lula (48->49->50); a later AtlasIntel reportedly still shows Flávio ahead but narrowing. Market 0.235; momentum and 2022 Lula-overstatement roughly offset, leaving Lula a clear underdog.
notes.adversarial: Routes to NO dominate: every poll but Datafolha/Vox has Flávio ahead (latest AtlasIntel 51.1–48.9, Quaest and PoderData 51–49, RTBD/Alfa 52–48; lead ≈ −1.8), 2022 polls overstated Lula's lead by 2.2 pp, the first round gave Flávio +1.9 with right-leaning remainder, and the $50m Polymarket sits at 0.235. Lula's Datafolha momentum (48→49→50) and Northeast machine are the only live YES route; lead −1.8 with sd ~2.5 gives ~0.24, slip 0.01.
notes.anchor: Anchor Polymarket 0.235 (re-read 17:20Z, unchanged, ~$29m volume). Poll model (lead -1.3, sd 1.345) gives 0.16 but sd is too narrow on n=3; with pooled sd 2.7 it is ~0.31; Datafolha trend toward Lula offsets the 2022 pro-Lula poll bias, so stay near market.
notes.outsider: Final polls are a coin flip (Datafolha 50-50, Quaest/PoderData 49-51) with a Lula trend, but Flavio led round one by 1.9 pp with the eliminated vote mostly right-leaning, 2022 polls overstated Lula, and the market gives Lula only about 23%.

cs.text: Vítěz druhého kola brazilských prezidentských voleb 25. října 2026 porazí druhého kandidáta o méně než 4,0 procentního bodu platných hlasů, podle TSE.
cs.criterion: ANO, pokud ve výsledcích druhého kola prezidentských voleb podle TSE (resultados.tse.jus.br / tse.jus.br) při 100 % sečtených okrsků, nebo podle posledního údaje TSE k 26. říjnu 2026 12:00 SEČ, činí rozdíl podílu platných hlasů vítěze a druhého kandidáta méně než 4,00 procentního bodu. NE, pokud je rozdíl 4,00 bodu či větší, nebo pokud se hlasování odloží či TSE do termínu výsledek nezveřejní.

base_rate.class: poll-lead model: P(|lead|<4) with lead ~ N(−1.33, 1.345)

notes.base-rate: The lead ~N(-1.3, 2.73) puts 0.81 of its mass inside |4|. Widened toward a 3.0 sd for the right-leaning miss risk (0.74). Two of three recent runoffs ended under 4 pp (2014: 3.28, 2022: 1.80). Less 1% slip.
notes.evidence: All late national polls put the gap at 0-2 pp and the first round gap was 1.87; only older Atlas/RTBD/Alfa showed 4+. Market <4% buckets sum 0.63; I lean above it given poll consensus and narrowing Atlas trend.
notes.adversarial: Lead −1.8 ± 2.5–3 puts ~0.74–0.80 of mass inside ±4, but the adversarial routes are real: polls clustered at 51–49 may be herding (AtlasIntel had +5.6 three weeks ago, RTBD/Alfa +4), a 2022-style Lula overstatement of ~2 pp pushes a Flávio margin to 4+, and the market prices the 4–8 Flávio bucket at 0.305. Shaded toward the market from the model.
notes.anchor: Anchor Polymarket sum of <4% buckets 0.63; polls (lead -1.3, even with sd 2.7) give ~0.82. Market prices a large Flavio 4-6% bucket (0.27), i.e. a 2022-style poll miss; moved partway toward polls.
notes.outsider: Polls point to a 0-3 pp race and recent runoffs were 1.8 and 3.3 pp; the main route to NO is a systematic poll miss toward Flavio of 4+ pp, which the market prices around 30-35%.

consensus.source: Mean of Datafolha 20–22 Oct (50), Quaest 17–20 Oct (49), PoderData/Aya 19–21 Oct (49); with AtlasIntel 3–8 Oct (47.2) 48.8. Final Datafolha/Quaest due Sat 24 Oct, not yet out.

forecast.scale_source: Half the pooled rms lead error of final polls (2.73 pp, 6 elections; pipeline/reference-data/poll-error.json) ≈ 1.3 pp per candidate share; the Datafolha-only figure (1.345/2 ≈ 0.7, n=3) is the narrow end. rms Datafolha final-poll runoff lead error 1.345 pp (2014, 2018, 2022; pipeline/reference-data/poll-error.json), halved for per-candidate share; n=3, narrow end (pooled party-error sd 2.61). Normal start q10 48.4 / q50 49.3 / q90 50.2.

notes.base-rate: Centre is the three-poll average of 49.3, shaded slightly for the historical right-leaning miss. The 80% band is ±1.7 pp of share, about 1.28 x (2.73/2).
notes.evidence: Late polls centre 49.3 with Datafolha at 50; market and older Atlas imply lower (~47-48) and 2022 polls overstated Lula by ~1 pp, so I shade the median to 49.0 and widen beyond the n=3 Datafolha error.
notes.adversarial: Centre on the seven-poll mean of Lula's valid share (~49.0) nudged down for the 2022 overstatement of Lula (+1.1 pp) and the first-round shortfall; width from a per-candidate sd ≈ 1.2 pp rather than the n=3 Datafolha 0.7, since AtlasIntel-style misses and herding are live.
notes.anchor: Polymarket specific-margin buckets imply Lula share q10 47.1 / q50 48.5 / q90 50.6; poll consensus 49.3 (sd 0.7 too narrow). Blend centred 48.9 with market-width tails; implies P(Lula>50) ~0.2, consistent with the win price.
notes.outsider: Poll average is 49.3% but polls overstated Lula in 2022 and the market's implied median is about 48.5, so I center near 48.9 with a spread of about 1.5 pp.

cs.label: Účast ve druhém kole nad rokem 2022
cs.text: Volební účast ve druhém kole brazilských prezidentských voleb 25. října 2026 bude podle TSE vyšší než 79,41 % z druhého kola v roce 2022.
cs.criterion: ANO, pokud účast ve druhém kole (comparecimento, % voličů) podle TSE při 100 % sečtených okrsků, nebo podle posledního údaje TSE k 26. říjnu 2026 12:00 SEČ, přesáhne 79,41 %. NE, pokud bude 79,41 % či nižší, nebo pokud se hlasování odloží či TSE do termínu údaj nezveřejní.

notes.base-rate: In past runoffs turnout usually fell from the first round (2006, 2010, 2014 and 2018 all fell; only 2022 rose, by 0.36 pp). YES needs a rise of more than 0.49 pp from 78.92%. A polarised, tight race nudges this up from about 0.10.
notes.evidence: Needs a +0.49 pp rise from the record-low 78.92% first round; 2022's rise was only 0.36 pp. A tight polarised race helps, but market-derived ~0.29 and the arithmetic point to NO as more likely.
notes.adversarial: Needs a rise of >0.49 pp over the record-abstention first round (78.92%); runoff turnout fell versus the first round in 2010, 2014 and 2018 and rose only 0.36 in 2022, so 2022's own figure is near the ceiling. Only the presidential race plus six governor runoffs are on the ballot and the electorate includes more inactive registrants; a knife-edge race is the sole YES route.
notes.anchor: Anchor Polymarket-derived 0.288 (79.41 sits inside the 78-80% bucket, linear split). Needs +0.49 pp over the first round; 2022 rose only 0.36 pp and 2014/2018 runoffs fell, so slightly below the derived figure.
notes.outsider: Round-one turnout was 78.92%, so YES needs a rise of at least 0.5 pp; 2022 rose only 0.36 pp and earlier runoffs usually fell, though a polarised close race helps.

base_rate.class: SNS-led list ≥45% in parliamentary elections with sourced figures (2016, 2022, 2023)
base_rate.source: Insajder 2016 RIK 48.25%; biznis.rs 2022 Ipsos 43.6%; N1 2023 RIK 46.71%

notes.base-rate: Class rate 2/3 (2016, 2023 yes; 2022 no) is a poor fit with a united opposition; RIK's all-ballots basis needs ~46.3 on valid votes vs non-commissioned averages 44-45 (-0.5 logit), partly offset by SNS beating independent polls in 2023 (+0.3); slip/late-RIK risk ~2%.
notes.evidence: Market puts 45%+ at about 0.52, probably on valid votes. RIK's all-ballots basis needs about 46.3% of valid votes, which is above the non-commissioned poll average (44.3) and only reached by government-friendly pollsters. Independent polls understated SNS in 2023, which keeps this close; three searches found no newer polls.
notes.adversarial: RIK's all-ballots basis means the list needs ~46.3% of valid votes; only government-commissioned polls (Ipsos 47.4, Faktor 48.6) put it there, and at Vučić's own 4.1m turnout 45% would be a record ~1.85m votes for the list while a united opposition list caps the pool. Polymarket's 0.52 for ≥45 is on the wider valid-vote basis and worth ~0.42 in RIK terms; take ~0.04 for late or disputed RIK publication (2022/2023 came only Monday evening).
notes.anchor: Anchor: Polymarket normalised P(>=45%) 0.518. Moved down about 0.06 because RIK prints the share over all ballots, which runs about 1.3 pts below valid-vote shares (bucket density is about 0.08/pt, half-weighted since the market's basis is unverified), plus a small risk that RIK publishes late.
notes.outsider: Unaffiliated polling average ~44.3 and RIK's all-ballots basis shaves ~1 pt; SNS historically beats polls and the market (basis unchecked) sits near 0.5, so slightly below even.

Pokud RIK do té doby výsledky nezveřejní nebo budou volby odloženy, platí NE.

notes.base-rate: No historical class (no opposition list ever near 40); start from poll average 42.5 valid, minus ~1 pt for RIK's all-ballots basis gives ~41.5 against a 40 bar with sd ~3-4 (~0.65), shaded down for Serbian opposition tending to underperform independent polls and late-RIK risk.
notes.evidence: Poll average and market median are about 42.5. RIK's basis takes about 1 point off, so the list needs about 41% of valid votes; the market's 0.66 drops to roughly 0.55 on that basis. Past understatement of SNS by independent polls trims it a little more.
notes.adversarial: Independent polls (NSPM 44.5, CRTA 44.9, Birodi 48.5) clear 40 but Serbian opposition lists have historically landed below independent polls, and the two government-linked polls sit at 40.0 and 37.1 before the ~1-point RIK denominator haircut and higher invalid ballots with 16 lists. Market ≥40 (0.66, valid-vote basis) shrinks to ~0.58 for ≥41 valid; minus publication/annulment risk.
notes.anchor: Anchor: Polymarket normalised P(>=40%) 0.659 (median about 42.7). Cut about 0.04 for RIK's all-ballots denominator (about 1 pt lower, half-weighted) and possibly higher invalid voting with 16 lists, plus a small publication-timing risk.
notes.outsider: Non-commissioned average 42.5 less ~1 pt for RIK basis gives ~41.5 with a wide sd (~4); market 0.66 but the list-versus-polls history is untested and pollsters diverge.

consensus.source: Polymarket turnout buckets read 2026-10-23T17:02Z, normalised median ≈64.75, Normal fit mean ≈65.1 (https://polymarket.com/event/serbia-parliamentary-election-turnout); Vučić's 4.1m voters ÷ 6,450,523 registered ≈63.6%; 2023: 58.77%

forecast.scale_source: No record of Serbian turnout-expectation errors found; sd ≈4.1 pp derived from a Normal fit to the Polymarket bucket distribution (CDF 0.22 at 62%, 0.88 at 70%)

notes.base-rate: Reference class: 58.77 (2023), about 58.5 (2022), 56 (2016), 53 (2014) and 48.9 (2020). Anything above 60 would be a two-decade high. Shifted up for a highly mobilised contest (Vučić expects about 63.6, polls say turnout is rising, the market median is about 65), but held below the market because the voter roll may be inflated.
notes.evidence: Reporting (ANSA: all polls show rising turnout, above 60%; Vučić expects ~4.1m = 63.6%) and market median ~65 point up from 58.8 in 2023; I shade below the market for an inflated roll and the low recent baseline.
notes.adversarial: Last two parliamentary elections 58.5–58.8%, and no Serbian parliamentary vote since 2008 (61.3%) exceeded 62; the Polymarket median of ~65 looks like opposition optimism, and a padded roll (Rašuo) depresses measured turnout. Mobilisation and Vučić's own 4.1m (63.6%) justify a centre above the comparables but below the market.
notes.anchor: Anchor Polymarket-implied median ~64.8, Normal fit mean 65.1 sd 4.1. Shaded down ~1 pp for the 58.8% 2023 base, a possibly inflated roll and opposition-optimism in the market; Vucic's 4.1m implies 63.6.
notes.outsider: The market median is about 65% and Vucic implies about 63.6%, but the last two parliamentary votes were about 58.5-58.8% and a disputed inflated voter roll pulls measured turnout down, so I center slightly below the market with a wide spread.

cs.label: Vallo obhájí post primátora Bratislavy
cs.text: Matúš Vallo obhájí v komunálních volbách 24. října post primátora Bratislavy podle výsledků Statistického úřadu SR zveřejněných do 25. října 18:00 SEČ.

NE, pokud víc hlasů dostal jiný kandidát nebo pokud jsou volby v Bratislavě odloženy či výsledek do termínu nezveřejněn.

notes.base-rate: Final-poll-leader class 5/6 and a 7-pt lead with realistic local sd ~6 give ~0.88; incumbent with 60% in 2022; market 0.91; slight discount for the single 19-day-old n=500 poll.
notes.evidence: An incumbent who won 60% in 2022, in a strongly anti-Smer capital; the only poll (AKO, early Oct) has him 7 points ahead and Polymarket has 0.91. The poll is a single n=500 one, 19 days old, and Šubová is splitting the vote, so I shade below the market. No newer poll found.
notes.adversarial: A single n=500 AKO poll 19 days old with a 7-point lead and 18% undecided is the whole evidence base; Ráž has a ministry and the governing coalition's machine in a 37%-turnout race, and an overlapping-interval poll can miss by more than 7. Bratislava's anti-Smer profile, Vallo's 60% in 2022 (polls then under-stated him), a possible Šubová withdrawal in his favour and a generous publication deadline keep this a clear but not safe favourite; Polymarket's 0.91 on thin volume looks a touch rich.
notes.anchor: Anchor: Polymarket 0.908. The lead model with a single n=500 poll lead of 7 and a realistic sd of 6.5 gives 0.86. Blended toward the market.

Uniform swing would flip several close Metro Vancouver and Surrey ridings, and the market has the Conservatives winning most seats at 0.925. The main NO path is a 44-46-seat plurality from inefficient Interior votes or a polling miss toward the NDP.
notes.adversarial: The Writ's 22 Oct projection (fetched) has the Conservatives at 53 seats on a 3.7-point lead but winning most seats in only 77% of simulations, so a majority is lower still; Angus Reid's latest is a 'statistical tie', BC polls over-stated the Conservatives in 2024, OneBC splits the right in Interior seats and the NDP vote is more efficient, so a plurality-minority (as in 2024's reverse) is a live NO path. Polymarket's 0.925 is for most seats, not 47, and looks over-priced; preliminary 'leading' counts at 04:00 PDT should be near-complete, so publication risk is small.
notes.anchor: Model: the October poll average gives Con +4. In 2024 a 1.6-pt NDP lead gave the NDP exactly 47 seats, and the Conservative vote is less efficient, so a majority needs about a +2 lead (lead 2/3.5 gives 0.72). The most-seats market at 0.925 implies a lead of about +5, which supports this. The main NO path is a plurality of 44-46 seats.
notes.outsider: Con ~92% for most seats with a ~4-pt vote lead, but 47 needs a majority and 2024 showed a small vote lead is a thin seat margin; roughly 0.63 conditional on most seats.

Uznání porážky nebo předání funkce premiéra bez zmínky o odchodu z čela strany se nepočítá. NE v ostatních případech, včetně vítězství NDP nebo odložení voleb.

notes.base-rate: P(NDP loses) ~0.9 (market 0.925); recent defeated premiers split between election-night resignations (Stefanson 2023, Higgs 2024) and 'reflect then quit' (Clark 2017, Gallant 2018, Notley stayed), so ~0.4 conditional; young leader, close race/minority scenario favours delay: 0.9*0.37.
notes.evidence: NDP loss ~0.9 per Polymarket; conditional on loss, an explicit leadership-exit statement within ~12h is maybe 35-40% (Higgs, Stefanson, MacLauchlan did so on the night; Clark, Gallant, Notley did not), and close polls make a narrow result where he stays or 'reflects' plausible.
notes.adversarial: Final polls (Angus Reid 'narrows', Liaison 43/37) leave NDP ~15% to keep power; among defeated Canadian premiers roughly half announce leaving the leadership on election night and half 'reflect' for days; a close count with late-counted ridings or a Conservative minority gives Eby reasons not to concede or to stay on pending the house, and 'I will not lead us into the next election' wording is a NO trap. Snap-election blame pushes up, but 0.85 x ~0.4 lands near 0.35.
notes.anchor: Anchor Polymarket NDP-loss ~0.92 (Doerkson 0.925) times ~0.42 that a defeated Canadian premier says on election night/next day he will quit as leader (Higgs, Stefanson, MacLauchlan yes; Clark, Notley, Gallant, Rankin stayed); a close race or minority makes staying on more likely.
notes.outsider: About 0.9 chance NDP loses (market 0.925 Conservatives); a self-called snap election lost is a strong trigger for an election-night resignation (Wynne, Couillard style), but many defeated leaders say they will reflect, so roughly 0.45 conditional.

notes.base-rate: No club or grémium meeting is known for 23-26 Oct, and formal Senate nominations usually come closer to the November constituent session, after the new senators take the oath on 19 Nov. The prior for a formal resolution in a 3-day window is ~5%; a Monday-morning ODS grémium resolution adds a little.
notes.evidence: ČT24 (20 Oct) says ODS–TOP 09 will 'likely' nominate him but has not done so formally; the vote is only after the 19 Nov oath, and no club or grémium meeting is reported before Monday noon. A Monday-morning ODS grémium resolution is the only realistic route.
notes.adversarial: Nothing is scheduled: the club is only re-constituted after the 19 Nov oath, ČT24 on 20 Oct said 'not yet a formal nomination', and Kupka's 'he will remain' type statements fail the vote/resolution test; the only YES route is a Monday-morning ODS grémium resolution reported before noon, or media loosely calling an intention a 'nomination'.
notes.anchor: No market exists. The anchor is ČT24: nomination 'likely' but not formal, new senators sworn in 19 Nov, leadership vote later in November. A formal resolution in a 3-day window over a weekend is unlikely; only a Monday-morning ODS executive meeting could produce one.
notes.outsider: Formal club vote is expected in November after the 19 Nov oath; ODS only said he will 'likely' be nominated and no meeting is known for 23-26 Oct.
